Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 61
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: South Asian
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Agricultural Worker
  trauma_type: Rape
  pcl5: 72

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Animals: Dogs, Intrusive Memory: A memory of the event coming to mind suddenly, Sexual Situations: Sexual situations or intimacy
  Threat: Body Reacts Before Mind: My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think, Sleep Vigilance: I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert, Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
  Memory: Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning, Memory Replay: My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over., Reliving Event: When I remember the frightening event I feel like it is happening right now.

Vignette:
Sunita, a 61-year-old South Asian woman married to her lifelong partner Rajiv, has been an agricultural worker for over four decades. Her life was marked by daily interactions with nature and hard labor until the traumatic event that shattered her sense of safety and security. One evening as she returned from work, Sunita found herself confronted by a man who forcibly dragged her into a nearby field and raped her. The experience was so intense and overwhelming that it left deep scars on both her mind and body. Since then, Sunita has been plagued by intrusive memories and triggers that keep the event vividly alive. Intrusive memories of the rape have become an unwelcome companion in her daily life. A sudden memory might come to mind while she is working in the fields or even at home with Rajiv. The intensity of these memories can be overwhelming, leaving her feeling as though she is reliving the trauma all over again. When this happens, Sunita often feels like she has been transported back to that field, re-experiencing the fear and helplessness she felt during the assault. Sunita's triggers are particularly potent because of specific elements tied to the traumatic event. Dogs, for instance, had barked in the distance as her attacker approached, making them a constant source of alarm whenever she encounters them on walks or near her home. Sexual situations and intimacy have also become fraught with anxiety. She finds it difficult to be intimate with Rajiv without feeling like she is reliving that traumatic moment. This has strained their relationship, leading to long conversations where Sunita tries to explain why certain physical touch feels threatening. Sunita's body reacts instinctively before her mind can process the danger. For example, if someone approaches her unexpectedly while she is working in the fields, she might jump or feel a surge of adrenaline even before she realizes who it is. This heightened state of arousal makes simple tasks like socializing at work gatherings extremely stressful. Her sleep has been severely disrupted due to vigilance and anxiety. Sunita often struggles to fall asleep because she feels that staying alert will keep her safe from any further harm. As a result, she often lies awake in bed, replaying the traumatic event over and over again like a film loop. Her memories are so vivid that it's as though the rape is happening all over again each time they come up. Even casual touches can trigger intense reactions. Rajiv has noticed this and tries to be mindful of how he approaches her, but sometimes an unexpected touch can send Sunita into a panic attack. These episodes have led to several tense conversations where she explains that such sudden movements can instantly bring back the full memory without warning. Over time, these symptoms have taken a toll on both Sunita's personal and professional life. Her work performance has declined as she often finds herself distracted by intrusive thoughts and triggered by elements in her environment. The strain on her relationship with Rajiv is palpable; they spend less time together because she fears intimate moments might trigger another traumatic reaction. What frightened Sunita most was the constant feeling of vulnerability, a sense that at any moment something could happen to bring back that awful day. She had come to believe that there was no escape from these memories and triggers, that they would forever be a part of her life. It was Rajiv who finally convinced Sunita to seek help when he noticed the decline in her wellbeing and their relationship. He encouraged her to speak with someone who could understand what she was going through. Sunita is hopeful that therapy might provide some relief from these intrusive memories and allow her to reclaim a sense of peace and control over her life once more.
